proposals.reason: Vehicle margin went from 9.4% to 15.3% a quarter ahead of management's own target, cash flow turned positive and Q4 is guided to a profit; the stock took that over a soft volume guide, +11% on 3.5x volume closing near the high, and the 12-1 delivery figure should show a large step up from October because the guide was given with most of November known.

reasoning.what_changed: Q3 on 11-25 before the open: revenue RMB28.8B against a RMB26.6-28.0B guide, deliveries 99,964, gross margin 16.7% (11.0% in Q2), vehicle margin 15.3% (9.4%), net loss RMB310M (RMB1.7B in Q2), free cash flow +RMB2.0B, cash RMB88B. Q4 guide: 110,000-115,000 deliveries and RMB31.7-33.1B revenue, which one write-up puts 12-16% under what the market expected, with a return to profit. The stock gapped +6.6% and closed +11.0% at 11.84 on 3.5x volume; 12.02 in the overnight session at 8:38 PM CT.
reasoning.story: The bear case on Li Auto was a price war eating a premium brand's margin. The refreshed MEGA, i9 and i6 on in-house chips and batteries restored the margin in one quarter, and the market chose that over the volume guide, which is the opposite of how it treated the stock all year. Broker targets (a JPMorgan Sell at $10 among them) were set on the Q2 margin and have to be revisited. The delivery guide needs about 40,000-43,000 a month for November and December against 29,025 in October, and management gave it on 11-25 with three weeks of November in hand.
reasoning.chart: 11.84 at Wednesday's close after +11.0% on 3.5x volume, in the top third of the day's range and above its middle (11.20); 12.02 overnight (+1.2%). ATR about 3.9%.
reasoning.coming: Friday's half session (to 12:00 PM CT). November deliveries on Tuesday 12-1, session 3 of the plan. Weekly China insurance registrations on Tuesday. Broker notes on the print. The US tariff proposal on China (January at the earliest) for the group.
reasoning.case_against: The Q4 delivery and revenue guide was under expectations, one third-party source has weekly i6 orders fading from about 54,000 to about 17,000 in November, total China car sales are down about 25% on the year, about 69% of the buyback is spent, and an 11% day can be given back in a thin half session. It didn't win because the price reaction on heavy volume was to the margin, not the volume, the guide embeds real November numbers so the 12-1 print is more likely to confirm than to shock, and the stop sits under the reaction day's middle.

proposals.wrong_if: Li Auto reports November deliveries under about 36,000 on 12-1 (the Q4 guide needs 40,000-43,000 a month); or it lowers the Q4 delivery guide of 110,000-115,000 or the Q4 profit target; or two or more covering brokers downgrade it after the print, inside the window.
proposals.hedge_why: Hedged with FXI (correlation 0.44, beta 1.08), not outright or against the default SPY (correlation 0.16): the belief is Li Auto's own margin turn, and a China fund takes out the tariff-proposal and China-tape risk that would hit any Chinese ADR, which SPY does not carry; outright would add China beta into a 12-9 Fed hike.

proposals.reason: Lula named Bradesco's chairman Luiz Trabuco finance minister on Thursday and the Planalto confirmed he accepted; Brazil's index rose 6.1% with long rates down more than 50 bp, it is still about 20% under its October peak after the election selloff, and a re-rating of the fiscal risk premium on a confirmed appointment usually takes more than one session. Itau is the cleanest bank to hold it in.

reasoning.what_changed: Thursday 11-26, with the US closed: Lula announced Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi, Bradesco's board chairman, as finance minister from January 2027, and the Planalto confirmed in a note that he accepted (InfoMoney; Rio Times). The Ibovespa rose 6.1% to about 176,800, its biggest gain since the first round, the real gained about 2.9%, long-end swap rates fell more than 50 bp; Itau rose 6.4% in Sao Paulo, Bradesco 11.6%, Banco do Brasil 12.6%. Lula also signed the Moretti fiscal package (up to R$56B of savings in 2027). The ADR traded 7.32 in the overnight session at 8:38 PM CT, +6.4% from 6.94.
reasoning.story: Brazilian assets fell about 18-20% after Lula's re-election on the fear of an unanchored budget, with the Selic stuck at 13.75%. A banker as finance minister plus a signed fiscal package is the first evidence against that fear, and foreign holders who sold the election are underweight. Itau is the quality bank: ROE 23.6%, cost of credit steady at 2.7%, guidance kept; it carries the country re-rating without Bradesco's own questions (rising delinquencies, a chairman leaving, conflict-of-interest noise) or Petrobras's capex plan due this month.
reasoning.chart: 6.94 at Wednesday's close; 7.32 overnight on 28,880 shares, spread about 0.5-0.7%, which is the ADR catching up to Thursday's Sao Paulo close. +1.5 ATR on the day (ATR about 4.3%).
reasoning.coming: B3 trades a full session Friday; the US closes at 12:00 PM CT. Reaction from the PT and Congress to the pick, further cabinet names, the Focus survey Monday, Copom on 12-9 (the last day of the plan is 12-3). No Itau report until 2-3.
reasoning.case_against: The first day is priced: the entry is the catch-up price, a 6% index day often consolidates, the PT's Chamber leader has already said Trabuco may not be the best option, he declined this job in 2014, and he does not take office until January. An ADR that has moved 1.5 ATR from its close may be stood down by the entry rule and never trade. It didn't win because the appointment is confirmed, not rumoured, the fiscal package is already law, and the market is still a fifth under its pre-election level.

proposals.wrong_if: Trabuco withdraws or Lula walks back the appointment; or Lula names an economic team or sets terms that the Brazilian press reports as overruling him on the surplus target; or the long-end swap rates and the real give back Thursday's move (rates retrace the 50 bp, USD/BRL back above about 5.80) on political pushback, inside the window.
proposals.hedge_why: Outright, not hedged: what moves this is Brazil's fiscal risk premium, which no US fund carries (the best fit is XLC at correlation 0.39, SPY 0.24), so a hedge would add a second unrelated bet rather than remove one.
